adversarial_review.check: The projected Gibbs square root is an unnormalized spectral contribution; the complement and global state transfer remain explicit open quantities.
Thresholds E are fixed manifest inputs independent of oscillator dimension; rank and mass are recorded rather than silently identifying windows.
Tail spread ratios use only the ten registered dimensions and four tail rows; no cutoff limit is inferred.
Signed group, absolute pair aggregate and signed-to-absolute ratio are separately computed in each window.
Both lanes rebuild the reversed term order and check antisymmetry at every cutoff and beta.
Projected Gibbs square roots are inserted separately into all four energy-weighted legs; no commutation through the commutator is assumed.
Unnormalized window contributions and conditional normalized values are both reported; neither is called an infinite-volume state.
The independent lane reconstructs oscillator, support terms, spectral projectors and weighted legs without importing the primary module.
Global KMS transfer, common core, thermodynamic history, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
R359 checks exact finite counts, tail fixture arithmetic and scope only; spectral matrix evidence remains Python/open analysis.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite low-energy spectral-window stress. It is not a global KMS state theorem, cutoff-removal theorem, common-core construction, thermodynamic dynamics, OS/KMS/GNS result, mass-gap proof, continuum result, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or Clay closure.
decision_reason: A fixed low-energy window removes the high-occupation growth seen in the full energy-weighted coefficient on this finite two-site fixture: after the declared tail cutoff d=12, all tested E<=4 and beta values have a bounded finite spread. This identifies a live QFT-facing topology in which Gibbs/KMS tails are decomposed spectrally before common-core transfer. It is not an analytic uniform estimate: the window projector, local Gibbs state, fixed geometry, sampled dimensions and threshold are all finite, and the full state includes an uncontrolled complement.
finding: Primary and independent lanes each pass 187/187 assertions over 30 high-cutoff beta rows and 120 spectral-window rows. The integrated verifier passes 3213/3213 and Lean R359 compiles. Reverse-order residuals pass the declared tolerance. For the four fixed windows E<=4, every beta has a tail (d>=12) signed-weighted spread ratio and conditional spread ratio below the registered 1.5 threshold. The largest tail spread ratios are 1.2183929213757922 (unnormalized) and 1.2335104477603323 (conditional). Full d=24/d=3 endpoint ratios range from 1.0652454717485893 to 2.9939611319329735 depending on beta and E, while the corresponding window masses remain explicitly reported (minimum 0.240252108724294 and maximum 1.0).
method: Hold the exact two-site Q3 edge and source support {0,1} fixed while sweeping oscillator dimensions d in {3,4,5,6,8,10,12,16,20,24}.
For beta in {0.5,1,2} and fixed energy thresholds E in {0.5,1,2,4}, diagonalize the induced finite Hamiltonian and project its Gibbs square root to energies <= E.

Evaluate the unnormalized projected K^(1/2)-Gibbs signed group, its absolute pair aggregate, conditional normalized value, Gibbs mass, rank and tail mass; compare the forward group with the reversed term order.
Reconstruct the full table in an independent implementation and cross-check grid counts, window counts, tail coverage, stability and scope in Lean R359.
next_action: Promote the fixed-window observation to an analytic spectral decomposition: prove a uniform Gibbs tail estimate for the complement, define the window/common-core interface independently of oscillator cutoff, and then test spatial-volume and source-translation dependence before any common-alpha promotion.
no_overclaim: Finite low-energy window stability identifies a live state-weighted route but does not prove a global KMS state, an unbounded common core, cutoff removal, a thermodynamic QFT dynamics, a mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.

qft_interface.closed: A finite fixed-energy spectral-window table for the signed Q3 union coefficient, with Gibbs mass/rank, reverse-order antisymmetry and high-cutoff spread diagnostics across three beta values.
qft_interface.open: A global KMS-compatible window decomposition, cutoff-uniform common-core estimate, actual Trotter defect, thermodynamic history, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference or Sector-A closure is supplied.

question: Does a fixed low-energy spectral window of the local Gibbs state suppress the high-cutoff signed-union coefficient on the two-site Q3 source edge?
title: Finite Q3 low-energy spectral-window state-weighted audit
